title: Yangwang U9 Xtreme sets a 312.65-mph production-car speed record
extract: BYD's electric hypercar reached 503.17 km/h on a closed road in Abu Dhabi, becoming the first production car to exceed 500 km/h in a single-direction run. Engineers adjusted its rear-wing angle, suspension rebound damping and tyre pressures between attempts; the four-motor U9 Xtreme produces nearly 3,000 hp.

title: FAA to finally ditch floppy disks in its air traffic control technology upgrade
extract: The Federal Aviation Administration plans to replace information display systems still dating to the 1980s across 435 facilities. The upgrade will retire floppy disks used to distribute weather, NOTAM and airport-status information, giving controllers a single, more accessible data platform.

title: Writer Nick Harkaway expands his father John le Carré's spyverse in new thriller The Taper Man
extract: Nick Harkaway's latest novel sends George Smiley to California in 1965 to pursue a Soviet agent and navigate tensions with le Carré's fictional CIA, 'the Cousins'. Harkaway says the Cold War setting has unsettling parallels with 2026, and plans at least one more Smiley novel.

title: True North by Paul Theroux review – an American's view of Canada
extract: Paul Theroux's latest travel book follows a long road journey across Canada, combining encounters with people from many walks of life with reflections on the country's identity, immigration and Indigenous history. The review finds the veteran travel writer's curiosity and energy undimmed at 85.

title: If Dune is this generation's Star Wars, we are all in big trouble
extract: Ben Child questions Florence Pugh's comparison of Denis Villeneuve's Dune films with Star Wars, contrasting the latter's hopeful rebellion and redemption with Dune's darker portrait of charismatic power, fanaticism and a ruler who may foresee catastrophe without preventing it.

title: The Cat in the Hat review – Bill Hader brings plenty but this animated rework is a mess
extract: Bill Hader and Matt Berry bring energy to Warner Bros' animated Dr Seuss adaptation, but the review argues that its overlong story borrows too heavily from other animated hits and turns the book's playful world into corporate workplace satire. A new Looney Tunes short featuring Daffy Duck screens before the film.

title: Rocky review – 50 years on, Stallone's boxer remains an exhilaratingly gritty contender
extract: The 1976 film returns for its 50th anniversary, with Peter Bradshaw praising its idealism, simplicity and enduring underdog appeal. Sylvester Stallone's Rocky Balboa remains a working-class fighter whose moral victory and determination to go the distance give the film its lasting emotional force.

title: I Play Rocky review – Anthony Ippolito adds knockout sweetness to the story of Stallone's Hollywood triumph
extract: This drama recounts how the young Sylvester Stallone refused lucrative offers to sell his Rocky screenplay unless he could play the lead himself. Anthony Ippolito is praised for capturing Stallone's warmth, humour and determination in a brisk, entertaining account of the film's unlikely creation.
